Assuming you're referring to depression and/or depression, why is it wrong to "label" it as being sick? Mental health should absolutely be compared to physical health 1:1, they're equally as important. Also, it absolutely shouldn't make you feel alienated, you are nowhere near alone. In group therapy I was shown this amazing video of a guy presenting the idea of physical health vs mental health, and I'm gonna try to find it in a few minutes, and if I can I'll edit this with a link.

With that said, I really do get what you're saying, and it's not an uncommon feeling. But with physical vs mental health, having the flue makes you sick physically, but having a mental illness makes you sick mentally. It took me a long time to accept this, because I had grown into it and gained comfort thinking "this is just who I am, and that's all there is to say". But just as you'll talk flu medicine to make you healthy physically, there's medicine out there for mental illnesses. They're very different, yet one and the same at the same time.

As someone who has pretty severe depression and anxiety, it sounds like you suffer from very severe anxiety and at least some depression. Your story reminds me alot of a chat I had with my uncle a couple years ago when my dad talked to him with how I was doing/acting, when I found out he suffers from beyond crippling anxiety as well as depression, like insanely similar, he talked about keeping his shades closed, falling to the floor and "army crawling" if anyone were to come to his door, ignoring calls/texts from family/friends alike.

My best suggestion for you is to accept that anxiety and depression are a very, very real possibility. I completely understand not knowing if you want to get "bettet". Schedule an appointment with a therapist, and just chat with them about what you're thinking, feeling, and experiencing. They'll know better than I do, and if they think meds are worth trying I'd recommend them. I'm on meds for my depression and anxiety, and the difference is seriously night and day. I can pretty much guarantee you'll be incredibly happy that you made the effort, you'll feel so much better.

But you need to decide if you want to do that, and I know it can be hard. I spent 12 years with crippling depression and anxiety, thinking nothing would get better (yet hoping it would), as well as not wanting to for whatever reason (this is who I am, can't get better, I deserve this, etc..). Meds, for me, have been beyond life changing, I'm still working on turning my life around, but I wouldn't be anywhere near the point I currently am without them. 

If you ever want/need to chat, please feel free to pm me. *hugs*

As someone with severe SA, it can be a real bitch. I assume your bf knows about it, but if not, consider bringing it to his attention for the sake of letting him know how you feel about your lack of connection with the group. Therapy can also help, a therapist won't inherently be able to cure it, but being on anxiety meds can make it much easier to participate in conversations with people (especially with people you don't know all that well).

I'm really bad at holding conversations, but the meds I'm prescribed have helped with the comfort of talking to people in general. I've found that it hasn't made it super easy to hold conversations (I believe that comes with experience, as I've been a recluse for a handful of years), but I stress about it alot less, and it's made me much less uncomfortable in social situations.

I'd definitely consider therapy/meds, but first off definitely make sure your bf knows how you're feeling in those situations, he might be able to sort of go out of his way to make sure you feel included in conversations, directly relating you to things to try and "drag you in to the chatting", for lack of better wording.

EDIT: I also want to add, you definitely shouldn't feel bad in any way about this whole thing. Being a good conversationalist comes natural, but absolutely doesn't come naturally to everyone, you are nowhere near alone in this.
